title: AAPS 3.4.1.0 Omnipod Dash didn't set the Profile on Pod Activation
body:
Hello,
I updated AAPS to version `3.4.1.0` yesterday (08.03.2026).
This morning I activated a new Omnipod Dash Pod (after 6:45 on 09.03.2026).
I didn't notice anything unusual, but when I tried to administer a bolus an hour later (around 07:40 on 09.03.2026), it didn't work and showed me an error that "Profile is not set".

I tried to apply the profile manually - it didn't help. After a few attempts, the pod started to scream. I reverted to an old version (`3.4.0.0`) and then successfully activated a new pod.

Unfortunately, I am not sure if a new version caused an issue. Something like that happened for me only once in the last 4 years, and that was not after an activation of the pod, but after a day or two of usage (the pod also started screaming and stopped working).

Sorry if that is just a bad coinsidence.

[AndroidAPS.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25850101/AndroidAPS.log)

comments.body:
## Log Analysis

Analyzed the attached log file. Here's the timeline:

| Time | Event |
|------|-------|
| 06:55:33 | Pod activation part 1 completed |
| 06:57:03 | Pod activation part 2 completed |
| 06:57:06 | Temp basal set (1.35 U/hr) — **pod working normally** |
| 07:21:56 | Temp basal set (1.35 U/hr) — **still working** |
| 07:31:13 | Temp basal set (2.7 U/hr) — **still working** |
| 07:34:53 | Temp basal set (3.3 U/hr) — **still working** |
| 07:37:18 | User requests bolus (1.0U) |
| 07:37:21 | `TREATMENT Pump UNKNOWN` — command result uncertain |
| 07:37:27 | `SUSPEND Loop` — pod entered error state |
| 07:38:04 | `IllegalStateException: Pod is in an incorrect state` |
| 07:38:04+ | All subsequent commands fail (bolus, profile switch attempts) |

### What happened

The pod worked correctly for **38 minutes** after activation. Then during a bolus attempt at 07:37, the pod entered hardware **ALARM** state. After that, `observePodRunning` correctly blocks all commands because `PodStatus.ALARM.isRunning() == false`.

The "Profile is not set" error the user saw is AAPS's response to the pod being in alarm — it cannot program anything on a pod that is no longer running.

### Not a code regression

- `OmnipodDashManagerImpl.kt` (where the check lives) is **identical** between `dev` and `compose` branches — no logic changes
- Recent Dash commits in `dev` are only BLE driver refactoring (PR #4604), not activation/running logic changes
- The pod functioned normally for 38 minutes before the alarm
- The `TREATMENT Pump UNKNOWN` at 07:37:21 suggests a communication failure during bolus — likely an occlusion or other hardware pod alarm

This appears to be a **pod hardware failure** (occlusion alarm, etc.) rather than a software regression. The user's own assessment ("Sorry if that is just a bad coincidence") seems correct.
